# Tikamātikā (Ds 1.1)

**Section:** Dhammasaṅgaṇī (ds)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tikamātikā* (Ds 1.1) forms the opening section of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the first treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhammapiṭaka [Buswell & Lopez 2014; Olivelle 2009]. It sets forth a matrix or schedule of triads (*tika*), consisting of twenty-two threefold classifications of phenomena (*dhammā*) that serve as the primary structural and doctrinal scaffold for both the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* and subsequent canonical Abhidhamma treatises such as the *Vibhaṅga*, *Dhātukathā*, and *Paṭṭhāna* [Buswell & Lopez 2014; Nyanatiloka 2007; Olivelle 2009]. The matrix begins with the fundamental triad of wholesome (*kusalā*), unwholesome (*akusalā*), and undetermined or neutral (*avyākatā*) qualities [Buswell & Lopez 2014; Olivelle 2009; Watanabe 1983]. Its triads are systematically demarcated into those of unlimited scope (*nippadesa*) and those of limited scope (*sappadesa*), encompassing classifications such as feeling (pleasant, painful, indifferent) and karmic results [Nyanatiloka 2007; Watanabe 1983].

Beyond scholastic analysis, the *Tikamātikā* holds a prominent liturgical role in Southeast Asian Buddhist traditions, particularly within communal chanting and funerary rituals in Cambodia [Walker 2018; Williams & Ladwig 2012].

DharmaNexus identifies extensive internal text reuse across the Abhidhammapiṭaka, recording 868 matches with 59 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its content is heavily shared with multiple sections of the *Paṭṭhāna*—especially the *Dassanenapahātabbahetukattika* (Patthana 1.10), *Dassanenapahātabbattika* (Patthana 1.9), and *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1)—as well as the *Khandhavibhaṅga* (Vb 1) and the *Tikanikkhepa* (Ds 2.3.1) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus algorithmically aligns segments of the text with Northern Buddhist scholastic treatises, including Sanskrit texts of the *Mahāyānasūtrālaṅkāra* and *Madhyāntavibhāgabhāṣya*, as well as Tibetan translations of the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* and the *Mahābherīhārakaparivarta Sūtra* [DharmaNexus].
